items.headline: U.S. Indices Decline Amid Weak Retail Sales and Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: Major U.S. stock indices ended mostly lower on Friday, August 14, pulling back from Thursday's record highs as weaker-than-expected retail sales data and rising geopolitical tensions weighed on investor sentiment. The S&P 500, NASDAQ, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all saw declines, while energy stocks rallied on higher oil prices.

items.headline: Eton Pharmaceuticals ($ETON) Soars on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Eton Pharmaceuticals ($ETON) surged 38% after reporting a strong quarter and raising its 2026 revenue outlook to over $145 million, targeting an adjusted EBITDA margin above 35%.

items.headline: Reddit ($RDDT) Jumps on S&P 500 Inclusion News
items.summary: Reddit ($RDDT) shares climbed 12.56% after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the social media company will replace AvalonBay Communities ($AVB) in the S&P 500, effective before trading opens on August 18.

items.headline: Nu Holdings ($NU) Rises on Robust Q2 Results
items.summary: Nu Holdings ($NU) saw its shares jump 13% following stronger-than-expected Q2 results, driven by a 56% year-over-year revenue increase to $5.88 billion and continued customer growth.

items.headline: Applied Materials ($AMAT) Falls Despite Upbeat Forecast
items.summary: Applied Materials ($AMAT) declined 5.12% even after delivering an upbeat quarterly forecast. Investors reacted negatively, suggesting expectations were already high due to strong AI-driven demand.

items.headline: Broadcom ($AVGO) Slips on AI Valuation Concerns
items.summary: Chipmaker Broadcom ($AVGO) shares fell 5.94%, reflecting broader investor nervousness about high valuations in AI-related stocks after pulling back from recent gains.

items.headline: Globant ($GLOB) Sinks on Disappointing Earnings
items.summary: Globant ($GLOB) shares dropped 5.8% after the IT and software development company delivered a disappointing second-quarter earnings report.

items.headline: Retail Sales Decline Signals Consumer Slowdown
items.summary: U.S. retail sales unexpectedly fell 0.6% in July, marking the largest monthly drop in over a year and missing economists' forecasts. This data contributed to concerns about consumer spending momentum starting to soften.

items.headline: Soft Inflation Data Eases Fed Rate Hike Concerns
items.summary: Softer-than-expected Producer Price Index (PPI) data for July, coupled with an in-line Consumer Price Index (CPI) reading, eased fears that the Federal Reserve would need to implement another rate hike in September. This provides some macro relief for equity markets.

items.headline: Middle East Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher, Impact Market
items.summary: Escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, with reports of two more ships attacked, fueled market pessimism and contributed to a rise in oil prices. The S&P 500 energy index rallied 1.4% on the news.

items.headline: Energy Leads, Healthcare Lags in Sector Performance
items.summary: Energy was the top-performing sector, gaining 1.36% on the day and 7.57% for the week, driven by higher oil prices. In contrast, the healthcare sector was the worst performer, declining 0.60% as investors rotated towards energy and memory stocks.
